<h5 align="left"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>OCEAN SHORE HOLDING CO. AND SUBSIDIARIES </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued) </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>FOR THE YEARS ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2008, 2007 AND 2006 </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">
<FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">not require any new fair value measurements. The definition of fair value retains the exchange price notion in earlier definitions of fair value. SFAS
No.&nbsp;157 clarifies that the exchange price is the price in an orderly transaction between market participants to sell the asset or transfer the liability in the market in which the reporting entity would transact for the asset or liability. The
definition focuses on the price that would be received to sell the asset or paid to transfer the liability (an exit price), not the price that would be paid to acquire the asset or received to assume the liability (an entry price). SFAS No.&nbsp;157
emphasizes that fair value is a market-based measurement, not an entity-specific measurement. FASB Staff Position (&#147;FSP&#148;) No.&nbsp;157-2, <I>Effective Date of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;157</I>, issued in February 2008, delays the effective
date of SFAS No.&nbsp;157 for nonfinancial assets and nonfinancial liabilities, except for items that are recognized or disclosed at fair value in an entity&#146;s financial statements on a recurring basis (at least annually), to fiscal years
beginning after November&nbsp;15, 2008. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">SFAS No.&nbsp;157 describes three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value:
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Level 1&#151;Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Level 2&#151;Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in
markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Level 3&#151;Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the
assets or liabilities. Level 3 assets and liabilities include financial instruments whose value is determined using pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies, or similar techniques, as well as instruments for which the determination of fair
value requires significant management judgment or estimation. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, SFAS No.&nbsp;157 requires the Company to disclose the fair
value for financial assets on both a recurring and non-recurring basis. The Company currently measures restricted equity investments on a non-recurring basis. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Those assets which will continue to be measured at fair value on a recurring basis are as follows: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>FOR THE YEARS ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2008, 2007 AND 2006 </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;107, <I>Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial Instruments</I>,
the Company is required to disclose the fair value of financial instruments. The fair value of a financial instrument is the current amount that would be exchanged between willing parties, other than in a distressed sale. Fair value is best
determined using market observable market prices, however for many of the Company&#146;s financial instruments no quoted market prices are readily available. In instances where quoted market prices are not readily available, fair value is determined
using present value or other techniques appropriate for the particular instrument. These techniques involve some degree of judgment and as a result are not necessarily indicative of the amounts the Company would realize in a current market exchange.
Different assumptions or estimation techniques may have a material effect on the estimated fair value. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

have a readily determinable fair value as its ownership is restricted and it lacks a market. The estimated fair value approximates the carrying amount. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

Accounts</I></B><I>&#151;</I>The fair value of NOW and other demand deposit accounts and passbook savings and club accounts is the amount payable on demand at the reporting date. The fair value of certificates is estimated by discounting future cash
flows using interest rates currently offered on certificates with similar remaining maturities. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Advances from FHLB</I></B>&#151;The

Under Agreements to Repurchase</I></B>&#151;The fair value is estimated by discounting future cash flows using current interest rates on agreements with similar remaining maturities. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Junior Subordinated Debenture</I></B>&#151;The fair value was estimated by discounting approximate cash flows of the borrowings by yields
estimating the fair value of similar issues. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Commitments to Extend Credit and Letters of Credit</I></B>&#151;The majority of the
Bank&#146;s commitments to extend credit and letters of credit carry current market interest rates if converted to loans. Because commitments to extend credit and letters of credit are generally unassignable by either the Bank or the borrower, they
only have value to the Bank and the borrower. The estimated fair value approximates the recorded deferred fee amounts, which are not significant. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">The fair value estimates presented herein are based on pertinent information available to management as of December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007. Although management is not aware of any factors that would significantly affect the fair value
amounts, such amounts have not been comprehensively revalued for purposes of these consolidated financial statements since December&nbsp;31, 2008 and 2007, and, therefore, current estimates of fair value may differ significantly from the amounts
presented herein. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>17. RELATED PARTY TRANSACTION </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>OCEAN SHORE HOLDING CO. AND SUBSIDIARIES </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS&#151;(Continued) </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>FOR THE YEARS ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2008, 2007 AND 2006 </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>19. SECOND STEP CONVERSION </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On August&nbsp;20, 2008, the Company, the Bank and OC Financial MHC adopted a Plan of Conversion and Reorganization (the &#147;Plan of Conversion&#148;) pursuant to which the Bank will reorganize from the two-tier
mutual holding company structure to the stock holding company structure. Pursuant to the Plan of Conversion, (i)&nbsp;OC Financial MHC and the Company each will convert to a federal interim stock association and then merge with and into the Bank,
with the Bank being the surviving entity, (ii)&nbsp;the Bank will merge with an interim subsidiary of a newly formed New Jersey corporation named Ocean Shore Holding Co., (iii)&nbsp;the shares of common stock of the Company held by persons other
than OC Financial MHC (whose shares will be canceled) will be converted into shares of common stock of new Ocean Shore Holding Co. pursuant to an exchange ratio designed to preserve the percentage ownership interests of such persons, (iv)&nbsp;the
Bank will issue all of its capital stock to new Ocean Shore Holding Co., and (v)&nbsp;new Ocean Shore Holding Co. will offer and sell shares of the common stock to depositors of the Bank and others in the manner and subject to the priorities set
forth in the Plan of Conversion. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the conversion and offering, shares of the Company&#146;s common stock currently owned
by OC Financial MHC will be canceled and new shares of common stock, representing the approximate 57.2% ownership interest of OC Financial MHC, will be offered for sale by new Ocean Shore Holding Co. Concurrent with the completion of the conversion
and offering, the Company&#146;s existing public shareholders will receive shares of new Ocean Shore Holding Co.&#146;s common stock for each share of the Company&#146;s common stock they own at that date, based on an exchange ratio to ensure that
they will own approximately the same percentage of the new Ocean Shore Holding Co.&#146;s common stock as they owned of the Company&#146;s common stock immediately prior to the conversion and offering. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At the time of the conversion, the Bank will establish a liquidation account in an amount equal to the greater of (a)&nbsp;the Bank&#146;s retained
earnings as reflected in the latest statement of financial condition used in the final offering prospectus for its minority stock offering or (b)&nbsp;the Bank&#146;s retained earnings as reflected in the latest statement of financial condition used
in the final offering prospectus for the conversion multiplied by the percentage ownership in the Company owned by OC Financial MHC. The liquidation account will be maintained for the benefit of eligible account holders and supplemental eligible
account holders (collectively, &#147;eligible depositors&#148;) who continue to maintain their deposit accounts in the Bank after the conversion. In the event of a complete liquidation of the Bank (and only in such event), eligible depositors who
continue to maintain accounts shall be entitled to receive a distribution from the liquidation account before any liquidation may be made with respect to common stock. The Bank may not declare or pay a cash dividend if the effect thereof would cause
its equity to be reduced below either the amount required for the liquidation account or the regulatory capital requirements imposed by the Office of Thrift Supervision. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The transactions contemplated by the Plan of Conversion were conditionally approved by the Office of Thrift Supervision on November&nbsp;12, 2008 and were approved by the shareholders of the Company and members of OC
Financial MHC on January&nbsp;8, 2009.&nbsp;If the conversion and offering are completed, conversion costs will be netted against the offering proceeds.&nbsp;If the conversion and offering are terminated, such costs will be expensed.&nbsp;As of
December&nbsp;31, 2008, the Company had incurred approximately $967,114 of conversion costs. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">89 </FONT></P>
